turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm glad you came in today. What brings you in?
turns.patient_response:
Well, thank you. I'm here because... ever since my choir friend passed away so suddenly, I just haven't been myself at all. 

I don't know, I find myself just crying over silly things, like the potluck lists. And I get all worked up about phone calls that I used to handle so easy. I've even started missing some of the church planning things... and I never, ever would have missed those before. I just can't seem to get a grip on things lately.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient reports developing emotional and behavioral symptoms, including crying spells, heightened anxiety over routine calls, and functional disruption (missing church planning), following the sudden death of her choir friend.

turns.doctor_question: Since your friend died, have you lost interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy?
turns.patient_response:
No, not really. I still enjoy the things I've always liked doing. I still want to be involved with the choir and my church groups... I still care about them just as much. 

It's just that I've been missing them because I get so overwhelmed and upset, not because I've lost interest or don't want to do them anymore.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies losing interest or pleasure in activities, stating that they still enjoy the things they like doing and want to be involved.

turns.doctor_question: Since your friend died, have you been feeling persistently nervous or worried?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't really say I feel nervous. I mean, I'm not sitting around worrying about things happening... it's not like that. It's more just that I get so easily upset and overwhelmed by the things I need to do. But no, I haven't been feeling persistently worried or anything.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies feeling persistently nervous or sitting around worrying about things happening.

turns.doctor_question: How long ago did your friend die?
turns.patient_response: She passed away just about a month ago. It was so sudden. And... well, it was only after that happened that I started falling apart with the church planning and getting so overwhelmed.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient explicitly links becoming overwhelmed and falling apart to the sudden death of her friend one month ago, indicating emotional or behavioral symptoms emerging in response to an identifiable stressor.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that your distress is significantly interfering with your ability to manage your usual daily responsibilities?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. It's really getting in the way. I've had to let some of the other church members step in and take over the phone calls, the planning lists, and... well, even parts of the luncheon we do. I'm just not keeping up with it all the way I always did before.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of reminders of your friend or her death, do you feel sad most of the day, nearly every day?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I miss her terribly, and thinking about her makes me cry... but if I'm just going about my day and not thinking about what happened, I don't feel sad all the time. It's just when she comes to mind, or when I feel like I can't handle things anymore. But no, not sad most of the day.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling sad most of the day or all the time outside of specific reminders of her friend.
